content.value_statement: Live meeting automation requires careful identity handling and separate identifiers. This skill guides authorized Lark discovery, participation, event reading, and communication through lark-cli.
actual_capabilities: Discover active meetings visible to the current user or an authorized application bot.
Join an active meeting as an application bot using a nine-digit meeting number.
Read paginated participant, chat, transcript, and content-sharing events from a live meeting.
Send authorized in-meeting text messages, reaction emojis, and video meeting feedback.
Leave a meeting as the application bot after an explicit user request.
limitations: The feature is in limited beta and requires eligible Lark accounts, application permissions, installation, and configured data scope.
It does not search ended meetings or retrieve participant snapshots, minutes, transcripts, or recordings.
Application event reading and messaging require the bot to be present or previously present within the supported grace window.
Operations require lark-cli, valid authentication, and correct handling of meeting numbers and long meeting IDs.

use_cases.title: Deploy a Meeting Assistant
use_cases.description: Join a confirmed live meeting, record its long meeting ID, and monitor events without leaving until requested.

use_cases.title: Monitor and Respond Live
use_cases.description: Review current speakers, participant changes, chat, transcripts, and shared content before sending an approved message or reaction.

use_cases.title: Discover Authorized Meetings
use_cases.description: Find active meetings visible to a user or application identity and preserve that identity for later event access.

prompt_templates.title: Find My Active Meetings
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the active Lark meetings visible to my current user identity. Show each title, meeting number, and long meeting ID.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner discovery of meetings visible to the signed-in user.

prompt_templates.title: Send Meeting Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: In my current meeting, send the reaction that means [feedback]. Confirm the selected meeting and reaction before sending.
prompt_templates.scenario: Send an approved reaction through the same identity used for discovery.

prompt_templates.title: Join and Monitor
prompt_templates.prompt: Join meeting [nine-digit number] as the application bot after confirming the number. Then retrieve all currently visible events and summarize them.
prompt_templates.scenario: Run a visible bot join followed by complete event retrieval.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze an Authorized Meeting
prompt_templates.prompt: Using application identity, discover meetings for [user open ID], let me choose one, fetch every event page, and summarize recent discussion and shared content.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced identity-aware discovery, selection, pagination, and content analysis.

output_examples.input: Which active meetings can my current user identity access?
output_examples.output: One active meeting is visible: Weekly Planning, meeting number 123456789. Its long meeting ID is available for event retrieval.

output_examples.input: What happened recently in the selected live meeting?
output: Two participants joined, one participant left, and the latest speaker discussed the release schedule.
A shared document appeared during the discussion. The summary includes its content only after authorized retrieval.
All available event pages were checked, and the latest page token was retained.

output_examples.output: The application bot joined the confirmed meeting and recorded its long meeting ID. Current visible events are ready for review.

best_practices: Confirm a nine-digit meeting number and its source before visible bot joins. Use dry run when identity or parameters are uncertain.
Keep the identity path consistent, and distinguish the nine-digit meeting number from the long meeting ID.
Fetch current events with full pagination before live-state answers, and request explicit approval for every visible write action.
anti_patterns: Do not treat any nine-digit number as automatic permission to join a meeting.
Do not reuse stale or partial event results when answering current meeting questions.
Do not use this skill for ended meetings, participant snapshots, recordings, minutes, transcripts, or bound group chat messages.

faq.question: What can this skill do during a live meeting?
faq.answer: It can discover meetings, join or leave as a bot, read authorized events, and send approved messages or reactions.

faq.question: Can it retrieve information from ended meetings?
faq.answer: No. Use the separate lark-vc capabilities for historical meetings, participant snapshots, minutes, transcripts, and recordings.

faq.question: Will the bot join when I provide a meeting number?
faq.answer: No. A meeting number becomes a join request only when you explicitly ask the application bot to enter.

faq.question: Which identities are supported?
faq.answer: User identity supports authorized personal discovery and access. Application identity supports bot discovery, participation, event reading, messaging, and leaving.

faq.question: What is the difference between the two meeting identifiers?
faq.answer: The nine-digit meeting number supports joining or matching. The longer meeting ID supports event reading, messaging, and leaving.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: You need lark-cli, valid authentication, an eligible Lark account, required application permissions, tenant installation, and configured data scope.
